navigation.title: Navigation and Shell Chrome
navigation.purpose: Global chrome surrounding every NusaShell view: title bar, sidebar, connection status, and storage indicator.
navigation.howToOpen: Always visible when the NusaShell window is open.

sections.heading: Title bar
paragraphs: Identifies NusaShell with its brand mark and wordmark, followed by compact backend connection status and a settings shortcut.

sections.heading: Sidebar
paragraphs: Vertical navigation on the left, ordered Home, Agent, Skills, Learning, Automation, Plugins, Providers, and Logs. It can show icons with labels or icons only, and remembers that choice locally.

sections.heading: Storage
paragraphs: Shows the absolute data directory path and a usage bar so the user can see where conversations, providers, memory, and credentials live.

home.title: Home
home.purpose: The launcher view: a grid of installed plugin apps. Each tile opens the plugin UI in a separate browser window. Searchable by name, id, or description and filterable by category.
home.howToOpen: Open NusaShell, or click the Home item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Filter row
paragraphs: A search input filters the app grid by name, id, or description. Category tabs narrow the grid to a single category. Escape or the clear button resets the search.

sections.heading: App grid
paragraphs: A responsive grid of plugin tiles. Each tile shows the plugin icon, name, and a runtime status when active. Clicking a tile opens the plugin UI in a new browser window sized from the plugin manifest.

agent.title: Agent
agent.purpose: The default view: multi-conversation chat against any configured provider model. Each conversation keeps its own history on disk and can use skills, memory, docs, plugin-provided MCP tools, and spawned ACP subagents.
agent.howToOpen: Open NusaShell, or click the Agent item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Conversations pane
paragraphs: Lists conversations with a search filter and a New conversation button. The count reflects persisted threads.

sections.heading: Thread
paragraphs: Renders the active conversation. An offline mascot appears when the backend is unreachable.

Long conversations open showing only the most recent messages, scrolled to the bottom; a 'Load older messages' button at the top of the thread reveals earlier messages in batches (keeping the scroll position anchored). Live streaming auto-follows only while the view is pinned to the bottom.

sections.heading: Tool call strip
paragraphs: Shows in-flight tool calls for the current turn, with one entry per MCP or built-in tool invocation.

sections.heading: ACP subagent dock
paragraphs: Appears above the composer when ACP subagents are live (or recently finished in this room). Each chip opens the right-hand drawer; the peek control opens a popup for one run. Drawer and popup support steer, stop, mode changes, and risk promotion. Permission prompts use a global overlay that stays visible across views.

sections.heading: ACP live views
paragraphs: The drawer lists every live spawn so you can switch between parallel subagents. The peek popup focuses one run. The permission overlay is fail-closed: timeout denies. Allow once, allow for this session, or deny.

sections.heading: Task checklist
paragraphs: A compact strip showing the agent's todo list for the current conversation. Items come from the `todo` tool; the user can delete items from the UI.

sections.heading: Steer queue
paragraphs: When a user sends a steer message mid-turn, it is queued here and applied at the next safe tool-round boundary.

sections.heading: Composer
paragraphs: The message input with attachments, model picker, workspace selector, provider status, stop, and send buttons. Ctrl+Enter (⌘↩ on Mac) sends.

skills.title: Skills
skills.purpose: Author and manage markdown instruction packs the agent can load on demand via `skill_run`.
skills.howToOpen: Click the Skills item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and a New skill button.

sections.heading: Catalog
paragraphs: Searchable list of installed skills. The count reflects persisted skills.

sections.heading: Editor
paragraphs: Edit the selected skill's name, description, and markdown content. Run opens the skill in a new Agent conversation as its system context. Save and Delete persist changes.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.purpose: Manage all plugins: manual MCP servers, MCP-only plugins, and MCP + UI plugins appear in one catalog.
plugins.howToOpen: Click the Plugins item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and two buttons: Add MCP opens the stdio server editor; Install plugin opens the plugin installer with catalog, GitHub, and ZIP options.

sections.heading: Plugin installer
paragraphs: A tabbed dialog for installing plugins. Catalog shows official first-party plugins. GitHub installs from a repository URL, optionally targeting a subdirectory for monorepos. Upload ZIP lets the user browse or drop a plugin archive.

sections.heading: Plugin window
paragraphs: Plugin UIs open in a separate browser window served same-origin at /plugins/<id>/ (the server injects the window.shell shim). Opening happens from Home tiles and the Plugins drawer Open UI button. The window is sized from the manifest ui.window (panel/widget request defaultSize with a 700x700 / 380x280 fallback; fullscreen opens a normal browser window). This keeps the plugin from covering or replacing the NusaShell UI. If the browser blocks the pop-up, a toast prompts the user to allow pop-ups.

sections.heading: Plugin catalog
paragraphs: Lists all plugins — manual MCP servers, MCP-only plugins, and MCP + UI plugins — with runtime state (idle/connected). Clicking a row opens the Plugins detail drawer.

sections.heading: Detail drawer
paragraphs: A right-hand drawer that opens when a catalog row is clicked. Shows the state machine, actions, preferences, tools, and manifest summary. Native MCP rows expose Start, Stop, Restart, Edit, and Delete; plugin rows expose Start, Stop, Restart, and Uninstall; MCP + UI plugins also expose Open UI. When a catalog plugin has a newer release, an Update button appears that updates it in place (plugin.update). Close with the X button, overlay, or Escape.

The Preferences area has an Auto start switch (shown for every entry) that launches the MCP server when NusaShell starts, and an Auto update switch (shown only for catalog-managed plugins) that updates the plugin automatically when a new version is released.

providers.title: Providers
providers.purpose: Configure LLM chat backends by wire format (Messages, Responses, Chat, Ollama, Codex) and spawn-only ACP subagent binaries. Chat API keys live in the local SQLite credential store. ACP env values stay on disk in acp-agents.json; the wire API only returns env keys.
providers.howToOpen: Click the Providers item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title plus Add provider (chat backends) and Add ACP agent (spawn-only subprocesses).

sections.heading: Chat providers
paragraphs: The registry lists LLM providers as cards. Selecting one opens the detail pane for editing the base URL, API key, enabled state, importing models, and testing connectivity. These models appear in the Agent composer.

sections.heading: ACP subagents
paragraphs: A separate registry for Agent Client Protocol binaries. Register a generic command + args + env. Probe discovers auth methods, modes, and models at runtime. ACP agents never appear in the composer; the parent agent spawns them with the subagent tool. Command is immutable after save.

learning.title: Learning
learning.purpose: Search accumulated memory entries and skills via hybrid BM25 + embedding + graph search, and explore how they connect in the knowledge graph.
learning.howToOpen: Click the Learning item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header stats
paragraphs: Live counts of memory entries and learning edges.

sections.heading: Search bar
paragraphs: Hybrid search across memory and skills, with a kind filter (All, Skills, Memory) and a Search button.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Ranked search results with a count. With an empty query the pane lists all skills and memories so content is visible immediately.

sections.heading: Knowledge graph
paragraphs: Force-directed graph (vis-network) of skills, memory entries, and their edges. Refresh reloads the graph; Fit fits it to view. Legend distinguishes Skill, Memory, Related, and Used-with edges.

automation.title: Automation
automation.purpose: Run workspace pipelines, manage durable once/every/when automations, inspect DAG runs, and see waiting or blocked states without occupying a runner.
automation.howToOpen: Click the Automation item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Header stats
paragraphs: Counts of runnable, blocked, and waiting automations so provider outages are visible without opening a run.

sections.heading: Toolbar
paragraphs: Tabs switch between Workflows, Runs, Schedules, and Events. The workspace field is used when starting .nusashell/pipeline.yaml. New automation opens a once/every/when/manual wizard. Run pipeline starts the workspace file.

sections.heading: Blocked provider
paragraphs: When a saved automation depends on a disabled MCP provider it stays BLOCKED rather than FAILED. Enable provider restores the binding without rewriting the workflow.

sections.heading: List and detail
paragraphs: The list shows the active tab. The detail pane renders job needs as a DAG, waiting wake times, and run/enable/disable/cancel actions.

logs.title: Logs
logs.purpose: Runtime events streamed live from the shell via WebSocket. The log file is a bounded ring (2000 entries) persisted as JSONL.
logs.howToOpen: Click the Logs item in the left sidebar.

sections.heading: Filters
paragraphs: Level filter (All/debug/info/warn/error), entry count, Follow toggle, and Clear button.

sections.heading: Tail
paragraphs: Scrolling list of log entries. When Follow is on, the tail auto-scrolls to the newest entry.

settings.title: Settings
settings.purpose: Control how this local NusaShell instance runs agent turns, manages context, picks embedding models, and presents the workspace. Browser-only preferences stay in local storage.
settings.howToOpen: Click the settings icon in the title bar, or press the Settings shortcut.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: View title and a Save settings button with a live status indicator.

sections.heading: Agent runtime
paragraphs: Default model for new conversations and the maximum tool rounds per turn (default 8). Existing conversations keep their selected model.

sections.heading: Embeddings
paragraphs: Embedding model used by skill and memory search. Models tagged as embedding-capable appear here after import. Ollama models (e.g. nomic-embed-text) work locally without an API key. The learning review threshold controls how many turns accumulate before extracting learnings (default 50, 0 disables turn-based review).

sections.heading: Vision fallback
paragraphs: When the active chat model cannot see images, NusaShell can describe attached images using a separate vision-capable model so the conversation continues without errors. Pick any model that supports image input. Leave disabled if you always use vision-capable chat models.

sections.heading: Context compaction
paragraphs: Toggle compaction, set max input tokens (fallback context window, default 200000), max output tokens (default 65536), prompt caching, and optional sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k, frequency penalty, presence penalty).

sections.heading: Appearance
paragraphs: Browser-only preferences stored locally, not sent to the agent.

sections.heading: Connection
paragraphs: Backend status, automatic reconnect toggle, and a Check connection button. The Go shell uses HTTP RPC for commands and WebSocket for live events.

sections.heading: System
paragraphs: Local diagnostics: version, data directory, and transports. This browser version does not manage desktop tray or login startup.

sidebar.label: Sidebar
sidebar.notes: Holds navigation items and storage indicator.

storage-path.label: Data directory path
storage-path.notes: Absolute path to the data directory.

search-input.label: App search
search-input.action: Filters installed apps by name, id, or description. Escape clears the query.

search-clear.label: Clear app search
search-clear.action: Clears the app search and returns focus to the search input.

launcher-tabs.label: App categories
launcher-tabs.action: Filters the app grid to a category.

app-grid.label: App grid
app-grid.action: Click an app tile to open its plugin UI in a separate browser window.

new-conversation-btn.label: New conversation
new-conversation-btn.action: Creates a new conversation and focuses the composer.

conversation-search.label: Conversation search
conversation-search.notes: Filters conversation titles in real time.

agent-offline-state.label: Offline mascot
agent-offline-state.notes: Shown when the backend is unreachable.

agent-thread.label: Thread log
agent-thread.notes: Renders the active conversation messages. Long conversations are windowed: only the most recent messages render on open (scrolled to bottom), older ones load on demand.

agent-load-older.label: Load older messages
agent-load-older.action: Reveals the previous batch of older messages at the top of the thread, keeping the scroll position anchored. Shown only while older messages remain windowed out; hidden once the oldest message is reached.

agent-composer-stack.label: Composer stack
agent-composer-stack.notes: Holds ACP dock, tool strip, todo strip, steer queue, and composer.

tool-job-strip.label: Tool calls strip
tool-job-strip.notes: In-flight tool calls for the current turn.

agent-todo-strip-list.label: Task list
agent-todo-strip-list.notes: Items come from the `todo` tool; user-deleted items disappear.

agent-steer-queue.label: Steer queue
agent-steer-queue.notes: Queued steer messages waiting for a safe boundary.

agent-file-input.label: File input
agent-file-input.notes: Hidden file picker for images, PDFs, and text files.

model-menu.label: Model menu
model-menu.notes: Lists models grouped by provider with effort chips.

agent-provider-status.label: Provider status / context usage
agent-provider-status.notes: Shows the backend context usage as used/window (e.g. 32k/1M). The number is the server source of truth: the live server-side estimate while a turn streams and the provider-measured context fill after it completes. The frontend never sums message bubbles.

stop-btn.label: Stop
stop-btn.action: Cancels the running turn; partial output is kept and marked interrupted.

new-skill-btn.label: New skill
new-skill-btn.action: Creates a new skill and opens the editor.

skill-run-btn.label: Run skill
skill-run-btn.action: Opens the skill in a new Agent conversation as its system context.

skill-content.label: Skill markdown
skill-content.notes: Injected verbatim into the agent context when loaded.

plugins-add-mcp.label: Add MCP
plugins-add-mcp.action: Opens the native MCP server editor.

plugin-table.label: Plugin catalog
plugin-table.notes: Lists all plugins with runtime status and tool chips. Clicking a row opens the Plugins detail drawer.

plugin-drawer.label: Plugin detail drawer
plugin-drawer.notes: Right-hand panel showing state machine, actions, tools, and manifest for the selected catalog item.

plugin-drawer-overlay.label: Drawer overlay
plugin-drawer-overlay.action: Clicking the overlay closes the drawer.

plugin-state-machine.label: State machine
plugin-state-machine.notes: Shows idle → connecting → connected → error with the current state highlighted.

plugin-btn-open-ui.label: Open UI
plugin-btn-open-ui.action: Opens the selected MCP + UI plugin in a separate browser window (served at /plugins/<id>/). Hidden for MCP-only entries.

plugin-btn-start.label: Start
plugin-btn-start.action: Connects the selected MCP server or plugin and lists its tools.

plugin-btn-restart.label: Restart
plugin-btn-restart.action: Stops then starts the selected MCP server or plugin.

plugin-btn-update.label: Update
plugin-btn-update.action: Updates a catalog plugin in place to its latest release (plugin.update). Appears only when a newer catalog version is available; the label shows the target version.

plugin-btn-edit.label: Edit
plugin-btn-edit.action: Opens the MCP server editor for the selected native MCP entry. Hidden for plugins.

plugin-btn-delete.label: Delete
plugin-btn-delete.action: Deletes the selected manual MCP-server plugin (plugin.delete). Hidden for installed plugins.

plugin-btn-uninstall.label: Uninstall
plugin-btn-uninstall.action: Uninstalls the selected plugin and drops its MCP connection (plugin.uninstall). Hidden for native MCP entries.

plugin-drawer-autostart.label: Auto start section
plugin-drawer-autostart.notes: Preference row shown for every entry; contains the auto-start switch.

plugin-autostart-toggle.label: Auto start
plugin-autostart-toggle.action: Launches this MCP server or plugin automatically when NusaShell starts (plugin.set_autostart).

plugin-drawer-autoupdate.label: Auto update section
plugin-drawer-autoupdate.notes: Preference row shown only for catalog-managed plugins; contains the auto-update switch.

plugin-autoupdate-toggle.label: Auto update
plugin-autoupdate-toggle.action: Updates this catalog plugin automatically when a new version is released (plugin.set_autoupdate). Shown only for catalog-managed plugins.

plugin-tools-list.label: Tools list
plugin-tools-list.notes: Lists the tools exposed by the connected MCP server or plugin with name and description.

plugin-tool-count.label: Tool count
plugin-tool-count.notes: Number of tools currently loaded for the selected entry.

plugin-manifest-info.label: Manifest info
plugin-manifest-info.notes: Key/value summary of the selected MCP server or plugin, including version, category, and install path when available.

provider-detail.label: Provider detail
provider-detail.notes: Edit form for the selected provider.

learning-graph-refresh.label: Reload graph
learning-graph-refresh.action: Reloads the graph from the backend.

learning-graph-fit.label: Fit to view
learning-graph-fit.action: Fits the graph to the viewport.

settings-learning-threshold.label: Learning review threshold
settings-learning-threshold.notes: Turns before review; 0 disables turn-based review.

plugin-install-cancel.label: Cancel install
plugin-install-cancel.action: Closes the plugin installer without installing.

plugin-install-confirm.label: Confirm install
plugin-install-confirm.action: Confirms the current install source (GitHub or ZIP).

plugin-install-error.label: Install error banner
plugin-install-error.notes: Inline error shown inside the installer when an install attempt fails; cleared on tab switch or dialog close.

plugin-catalog-search.label: Plugin catalog search
plugin-catalog-search.action: Filters the plugin catalog by name, id, or description.

add-acp-agent-btn.label: Add ACP agent
add-acp-agent-btn.action: Opens a generic command/args/env form to register a spawn-only ACP binary.

acp-agent-registry.label: ACP agent registry
acp-agent-registry.notes: Cards for spawn-only ACP binaries. Not shown in the Agent composer.

acp-agent-detail.label: ACP agent detail
acp-agent-detail.notes: Edit label/args/env, probe, authenticate, refresh catalog, and map advertised modes to risk tiers. Command is read-only after save.

acp-dock.label: ACP subagent dock
acp-dock.notes: Hidden until at least one live or recently finished ACP run exists.

acp-drawer-overlay.label: ACP drawer overlay
acp-drawer-overlay.action: Click to close the subagent drawer.

acp-drawer.label: ACP subagent drawer
acp-drawer.notes: Wider than the plugin drawer so a live transcript, steer box, and mode chips fit.

acp-popup-overlay.label: ACP peek overlay
acp-popup-overlay.action: Click outside the dialog to close the peek popup.

acp-permission-overlay.label: ACP permission overlay
acp-permission-overlay.notes: Global. Timeout denies. Stays visible if you leave the Agent view.

acp-permission-allow-session.label: Allow ACP permission for session
acp-permission-allow-session.action: Allows this tool and auto-allows later permission prompts on the same run.
